foundation.title: Foundation
foundation.subtitle: Decide what this wedding is before you decide what's in it
foundation.celebration: The hard conversations are done. Everything after this is easier.

set_total_budget.title: Agree on a total number
set_total_budget.description: The 2026 US average is about $34,200 for around 117 guests, roughly $290 a guest. Yours can be anything. What matters is that you both say the number out loud.

agree_who_pays.title: Sort out who's contributing
agree_who_pays.description: The old rule about the bride's family paying is mostly gone. Ask directly, and ask whether a contribution comes with expectations attached.

allocate_categories.title: Split the budget across categories
allocate_categories.description: A planner-standard split: venue and catering 40-50%, photo and video 10-12%, flowers and decor 8-10%, attire and beauty 5-9%, music 5-10%, rings 4%, stationery 2-3%.

reserve_buffer.title: Set aside 5-10% for buffer and tips
reserve_buffer.description: Gratuity is expected in the US and is not the same as the service charge on your catering bill. Budget it separately or it will surprise you.

open_wedding_account.title: Open a separate account for wedding money

write_couple_funded_guardrails.title: Write the guardrails for funding this yourselves
write_couple_funded_guardrails.description: Agree on the maximum total, what savings are protected, whether debt is off the table, and the amount either person can commit without another conversation.

confirm_family_gift_boundaries.title: Confirm that family contributions are gifts, not decision rights
confirm_family_gift_boundaries.description: Thank each contributor and say clearly whether the money changes the guest list, ceremony, vendors, or other decisions before accepting it.

write_family_input_boundaries.title: Write down what family funding can and cannot influence
write_family_input_boundaries.description: Name the decisions contributors may join, the decisions that remain yours, and what happens if expectations grow after money is committed.

clarify_family_contributions.title: Have the unfinished family contribution conversations
clarify_family_contributions.description: Ask for an amount, timing, and attached expectations. Build the plan only after an unclear promise becomes a clear yes, no, or number.

draft_guest_count.title: Draft a guest count
draft_guest_count.description: Not the list yet, just the number. It drives venue size, catering, and most of your budget.

pick_three_priorities.title: Each pick your top three
pick_three_priorities.description: Compare them. Where you disagree is where the real budget conversation is.

agree_non_negotiables.title: Write down what you will not compromise on

define_guest_experience_anchor.title: Define what a cared-for guest should experience
define_guest_experience_anchor.description: Write one sentence Bliss can use when choices compete: what should guests feel, and which practical details make that feeling real?

define_atmosphere_anchor.title: Define the atmosphere worth protecting
define_atmosphere_anchor.description: Name the visual and emotional qualities that matter. This becomes a filter for venue, design, flowers, lighting, and rentals.

define_food_party_anchor.title: Define what makes the meal and party successful
define_food_party_anchor.description: Name the energy, hospitality, food quality, music, and dancing experience you would protect before decorative extras.

define_meaning_tradition_anchor.title: Define the meaning and traditions worth protecting
define_meaning_tradition_anchor.description: Name the rituals, people, or cultural details that make this wedding yours rather than interchangeable.

define_low_stress_anchor.title: Define what a low-stress wedding means to you
define_low_stress_anchor.description: Name the complexity, spending, or obligations you are willing to remove so the process and the day still feel like yours.

decide_planner_level.title: Decide how much help you want
decide_planner_level.description: Full-service, partial, or a day-of coordinator. Note that a venue coordinator works for the venue, not for you, so it isn't the same thing.

buy_wedding_insurance.title: Look into wedding insurance
buy_wedding_insurance.description: Liability coverage is required by many venues, and cancellation coverage protects deposits.

map_domain_owners.title: Choose an owner for each planning domain
map_domain_owners.description: Ownership means doing the research and bringing back a recommendation. It does not mean hiding the decision or carrying the whole wedding alone.

define_two_yes_decisions.title: Name the decisions that require two yeses
define_two_yes_decisions.description: Choose the budget, guest, tradition, contract, and schedule decisions neither person should finalize alone.

schedule_weekly_planning_checkin.title: Schedule one short weekly planning check-in
schedule_weekly_planning_checkin.description: Keep it bounded: review decisions, blockers, and the next few actions, then stop talking about the wedding for the night.

write_decision_protocol.title: Write a simple rule for decisions that get stuck
write_decision_protocol.description: Each person states the need underneath their position, you name the shared constraint, and you compare one or two options against it before pausing.

funding_boundaries.prompt: What does family money mean in this wedding?
funding_boundaries.help: Money becomes conflict when the amount is clear but the expectations are not. Bliss will keep funding and decision rights separate unless you explicitly connect them.

option.family_gift: Family is contributing without decision rights
option.family_with_input: Family contributions come with agreed input
option.still_unclear: The amount or expectations are still unclear

tradeoff_anchor.prompt: When money or time forces a tradeoff, what should Bliss protect first?
tradeoff_anchor.help: This is not the only thing that matters. It is the anchor Bliss should return to when two good choices cannot both survive.

option.low_stress: A calm process and uncomplicated day

decision_rhythm.prompt: How do you want to make planning decisions together?
decision_rhythm.help: The goal is not equal labor on every task. It is visible ownership, known shared decisions, and a way to slow down when either person does not feel heard.

option.shared_big_decisions: We divide the work but make big decisions together
option.weekly_checkin: We decide during one weekly check-in
option.needs_structure: We need a clearer decision method

venue_date.title: Venue and Date
venue_date.subtitle: Lock the stage, and everything else gets a deadline
venue_date.celebration: Date locked, venue booked. Now the rest of the plan has something to hang on.

pick_season_and_range.title: Pick a season and a range of dates

check_family_conflicts.title: Check the date against both families

consider_offpeak_pricing.title: Price out Friday, Sunday, or off-season
consider_offpeak_pricing.description: Peak is May through October, Saturdays. Moving off it can cut venue cost meaningfully.

check_holiday_weekends.title: Check holiday weekends
check_holiday_weekends.description: They help guests travel and hurt hotel prices. Decide which matters more.

confirm_fixed_date_constraints.title: Write down what the fixed date rules out
confirm_fixed_date_constraints.description: A fixed date narrows the venue pool immediately. Name the date constraint so you do not keep falling for places that cannot host it.

compare_date_options.title: Compare two or three real date options
compare_date_options.description: Compare availability, price, travel impact, and the people who matter most before one date becomes emotionally fixed.

rank_venue_before_date.title: Agree that the right venue chooses the date
rank_venue_before_date.description: Set the season and hard conflicts, then let the best venue's availability decide the exact day.

write_venue_requirements.title: Write down what the venue must have

check_availability.title: Check availability for your dates
check_availability.description: Popular venues and peak dates book 12 to 18 months out.

audit_full_service_inclusions.title: Audit what the full-service package actually includes
audit_full_service_inclusions.description: List tables, chairs, linens, staffing, setup, cleanup, catering, and service charges. An inclusion only saves money if it is something you would otherwise rent or hire.

build_blank_canvas_cost_model.title: Price the blank canvas before falling in love with it
build_blank_canvas_cost_model.description: Add rentals, power, lighting, restrooms, staffing, delivery, setup, and teardown to the site fee before comparing it with a full-service venue.

confirm_restaurant_buyout_terms.title: Confirm the restaurant or hotel buyout terms
confirm_restaurant_buyout_terms.description: Ask about the food minimum, private-room boundaries, service hours, sound limits, and what other guests can access.

verify_outdoor_infrastructure.title: Verify the outdoor site's weather and infrastructure plan
verify_outdoor_infrastructure.description: Confirm the backup space, power, lighting, restrooms, accessibility, parking, permits, and the exact weather decision deadline.

book_tours.title: Book tours at your top three

tour_with_checklist.title: Tour with a checklist and take photos

ask_fb_minimum.title: Ask about the food and beverage minimum
ask_fb_minimum.description: This is separate from the site fee and is often the larger number.

ask_vendor_restrictions.title: Ask whether you must use their vendor list
ask_vendor_restrictions.description: An exclusive caterer or a closed vendor list removes choices you may want.

ask_coi_requirements.title: Ask what insurance certificates they require
ask_coi_requirements.description: Most venues need each vendor to carry liability coverage and name the venue on the certificate.

confirm_rain_plan.title: Confirm the rain plan and when the call is made
confirm_rain_plan.description: Ask to see the backup space. If you would not be happy getting married in it, you do not have a rain plan.

ask_overtime_rate.title: Ask the overtime rate and hard end time

confirm_room_flip_and_guest_flow.title: Map the ceremony-to-reception room flip and guest flow
confirm_room_flip_and_guest_flow.description: Know where guests go, who moves furniture, how long the flip takes, and what happens if weather removes the holding space.

measure_transfer_time_and_transport.title: Measure the real transfer between ceremony and reception
measure_transfer_time_and_transport.description: Drive it at the right time of day, add parking and loading time, and decide whether guests need shared transportation.

compare_one_site_vs_two.title: Compare one site with separate ceremony and reception sites
compare_one_site_vs_two.description: Compare meaning, guest friction, transportation, setup duplication, and cost before shortlisting venues.

compare_all_in_cost.title: Compare the true all-in cost, not the site fee

review_contract.title: Read the contract line by line

check_force_majeure.title: Read the force majeure and cancellation clauses
check_force_majeure.description: Know what happens, and what you get back, if the date has to move.

pay_retainer.title: Pay the retainer
pay_retainer.description: Usually non-refundable. This is the moment the date becomes real.

lock_the_date.title: Tell everyone the date is locked

date_flexibility.prompt: Which comes first: the date or the venue?
date_flexibility.help: A fixed date sharply narrows availability. A flexible window gives you leverage, while venue-first protects the place you care about most.

option.venue_first: The right venue can choose the date

venue_style.prompt: What kind of venue work feels right?
venue_style.help: A lower site fee can hide rentals, staffing, power, and setup. This choice changes what you must price and verify.

option.blank_canvas: A blank canvas we build ourselves

site_plan.prompt: Ceremony and reception in one place or two?
site_plan.help: Two meaningful locations can be worth it, but they add guest movement, transportation, and duplicated setup.

vendor_team.title: Vendor Dream Team
vendor_team.subtitle: The people who make the day actually happen
vendor_team.celebration: Your team is booked. These are the people who will carry the day.

photographer_choice.help: Choose only from photographers found through the verified shortlist. Bliss will show sourced strengths and concerns, never invented fit percentages.

define_photo_style.title: Decide on a photo style
define_photo_style.description: Documentary, editorial, film, dark and moody, light and airy. Naming it makes shortlisting much faster.

review_full_galleries.title: Ask to see full galleries, not portfolios
review_full_galleries.description: A portfolio is the best twenty frames of a career. A full wedding gallery is what you will actually receive.

book_photographer.title: Book the photographer
book_photographer.description: Book 9 to 12 months out. Good photographers go first, often before the venue.

book_content_creator.title: Consider a content creator
book_content_creator.description: A newer vendor category: someone shooting phone video for social, alongside your photographer.

decide_dj_or_band.title: Decide between a DJ and a band
decide_dj_or_band.description: A DJ averages around $1,700, a live band around $4,200. A band needs more space, more power, and more breaks.

audition_music.title: Watch live footage or attend a showcase

verify_officiant_credentials.title: Verify their credentials are valid in your state
verify_officiant_credentials.description: Some jurisdictions, including parts of New York, do not reliably accept online ordinations. Getting this wrong can invalidate the marriage.

book_officiant.title: Book the officiant and share your ceremony vision

book_day_of_coordinator.title: Book a day-of coordinator
book_day_of_coordinator.description: If you have no planner, this is the single highest-value hire. Someone has to run the day, and it should not be you or your mother.

collect_vendor_cois.title: Collect certificates of insurance from every vendor

build_vendor_contact_sheet.title: Build one contact sheet with every vendor on it

wedding_party.title: Wedding Party and VIPs
wedding_party.subtitle: The people standing next to you
wedding_party.celebration: Your people are in place, and they know what they signed up for.

decide_party_size.title: Decide how many people you want standing up

choose_honor_attendants.title: Choose a maid or matron of honor and a best man

ask_kid_attendants.title: Ask a flower girl and ring bearer

map_traditional_party_sides.title: Map each partner's wedding party
map_traditional_party_sides.description: Choose each side without forcing equal numbers. The people should fit the relationships, not a photograph.

build_one_shared_circle.title: Build one shared wedding-party circle
build_one_shared_circle.description: Choose people across friendships and families, then decide where everyone stands without labeling them by gender or partner.

name_small_vip_circle.title: Name the small circle you want closest
name_small_vip_circle.description: Keep the role meaningful and light: identify the few people you want beside you without building a large formal party.

define_vip_roles_without_a_party.title: Honor your VIPs without creating a formal party
define_vip_roles_without_a_party.description: Name the people who matter and choose optional moments for them, without attire rules, standing positions, or bundled obligations.

explain_duties_and_costs.title: Be upfront about what it costs them
explain_duties_and_costs.description: Attire, travel, showers, and bachelor or bachelorette parties add up fast. Saying the number early is a kindness.

name_a_point_person.title: Name a point person for vendors
name_a_point_person.description: One name and number every vendor calls on the day, so nobody calls you.

tell_party_presence_is_enough.title: Tell them their presence is enough
tell_party_presence_is_enough.description: Say explicitly that the role is celebratory, not unpaid labor, and that extra events or spending are optional.

agree_light_support_requests.title: Agree on the few ways you may ask for help
agree_light_support_requests.description: Name two or three bounded requests in advance so support feels chosen instead of expanding quietly.

confirm_active_team_responsibilities.title: Confirm responsibilities with each person
confirm_active_team_responsibilities.description: Match every concrete job to willingness, availability, and cost. A title is not consent to an unlimited workload.

set_party_attire_direction.title: Set the direction for their attire

share_palette_and_fit_guardrails.title: Share a palette and a few fit guardrails
share_palette_and_fit_guardrails.description: Give enough direction for the group to feel connected while leaving room for bodies, budgets, identities, and personal style.

review_existing_outfits_for_comfort.title: Review the outfits people already own
review_existing_outfits_for_comfort.description: Check comfort, weather, formality, and how the group works together before asking anyone to buy something new.

confirm_no_required_outfit_purchase.title: Confirm that no matching purchase is required
confirm_no_required_outfit_purchase.description: Tell the group what the venue and weather require, then let each person dress as themselves within those practical limits.

structure.prompt: Who, if anyone, should have a formal wedding-party role?
structure.help: Start with the relationships you want close, not symmetry, gender, or inherited labels.

support_level.prompt: How much responsibility should come with the role?
support_level.help: Clear, voluntary expectations protect the friendship. Bliss will not treat a title as consent to labor or spending.

option.celebratory_only: Celebrate with us; no jobs expected
option.active_team: An active team with named responsibilities

attire_direction.prompt: How coordinated should wedding-party attire feel?
attire_direction.help: Choose the amount of visual consistency that still respects budget, comfort, bodies, identity, and personal style.

attire_beauty.title: Attire and Beauty
attire_beauty.subtitle: Finding the one you'll cry over
attire_beauty.celebration: Everything fits. You already know how it feels to put it on.

set_gown_budget.title: Set a gown budget, including alterations
set_gown_budget.description: Alterations typically add several hundred dollars and are almost never included in the ticket price.

book_salon_appointments.title: Book two or three salon appointments
book_salon_appointments.description: Book them close together. Trying on dresses months apart makes comparison impossible.

order_the_gown.title: Order the gown
order_the_gown.description: Made-to-order gowns take 6 to 9 months to arrive, before alterations even start. This is the longest lead time in the whole plan.

first_fitting.title: First fitting
first_fitting.description: About 8 weeks out. Bring the shoes and undergarments you will actually wear.

learn_the_bustle.title: Teach someone how to bustle the dress
learn_the_bustle.description: Whoever will do it on the day should practice at the final fitting. Film it on your phone.

buy_undergarments.title: Buy undergarments before the first fitting

decide_suit_or_tux.title: Decide on a suit or a tuxedo
decide_suit_or_tux.description: Match the formality to the dress code you are asking guests to follow.

buy_accessories.title: Sort out shirt, tie, cufflinks, and pocket square

break_in_shoes.title: Break the shoes in
break_in_shoes.description: Wear them around the house. You will be standing for eight hours.

book_hair_makeup.title: Book hair and makeup
book_hair_makeup.description: Book 6 to 9 months out, and confirm they can cover everyone getting ready with you.

do_hair_makeup_trial.title: Do the trial
do_hair_makeup_trial.description: Schedule it near an engagement shoot or an event so you can see the look photograph and last.

book_party_beauty.title: Arrange hair and makeup for anyone joining you

plan_skin_timeline.title: Plan skin treatments backward from the date
plan_skin_timeline.description: Never try anything new inside a month. Whatever you do, do it early enough to recover from.

book_nails.title: Book nails for two or three days before

book_rental_appointments.title: Book a rental try-on appointment
book_rental_appointments.description: Rental houses hold a limited number of each size. Go early enough that your first choice is still available in your size.

reserve_rental_gown.title: Reserve the gown and lock the delivery date
reserve_rental_gown.description: Ask for delivery a week before the wedding, not two days. It leaves room for the small fixes a rental still needs.

confirm_rental_window_and_return.title: Confirm the return window and who returns it
confirm_rental_window_and_return.description: Late fees on rentals are steep, and you will be on a plane. Assign this to someone who is not you.

buy_the_gown_offrack.title: Buy the gown off the rack
buy_the_gown_offrack.description: You are walking out with it, so budget for alterations separately. Off-the-rack still usually needs two fittings.

choose_second_look.title: Choose the second look
choose_second_look.description: Decide it alongside the first, in the same light. Two outfits chosen months apart tend to fight each other in photos.

arrange_quick_change_help.title: Plan the quick change: where, when, and who helps
arrange_quick_change_help.description: A change takes ten to twenty minutes and a private room with a mirror. Put it in the run of show or it eats your reception.

reserve_suit_rental.title: Reserve the suit or tux rental
reserve_suit_rental.description: Rentals need measurements a month out. Book the whole party at the same shop so the fabrics actually match.

rental_pickup_and_try_on.title: Pick up the rental and try it on immediately
rental_pickup_and_try_on.description: Try it on at the shop, not at home. A wrong size discovered in the store is fixable that day.

custom_suit_measurements.title: Sit for made-to-measure measurements
custom_suit_measurements.description: Made to measure takes three to four months and one round of adjustments. Book the fitting before you order the fabric.

book_a_makeup_lesson.title: Book one lesson with a makeup artist
book_a_makeup_lesson.description: A single paid lesson is the cheapest insurance for doing your own face. You learn what photographs well, which is not what looks good in a mirror.

practice_the_diy_look.title: Practice the full look, photographed
practice_the_diy_look.description: Do it once, in daylight and in flash, and look at the photos. Camera flash finds every product a mirror hides.

dress_acquisition.prompt: Renting, buying off the rack, or having one made?
dress_acquisition.help: This one question changes the rest of this quest more than any other. Renting is a three-week commitment; a custom gown is six months.

suit_acquisition.prompt: And the suit or tux — rent, buy, or tailor-made?

beauty_approach.prompt: Who is doing hair and makeup on the day?
beauty_approach.help: Artists for the whole wedding party book up first and cost per head. Deciding now is what keeps this from becoming a scramble in the final month.

option.pro_team: A pro team for us and the wedding party
option.pro_for_couple_only: A pro for us two only

second_look.prompt: Planning to change into a second look?
second_look.help: Common for a reception entrance or a cultural ceremony. It needs a plan for where and who helps, not just the outfit.

guests_stationery.title: Guest List and Stationery
guests_stationery.subtitle: Naming the people who will be in the room
guests_stationery.celebration: Invitations are out. Now you get to watch the yeses come in.

set_plus_one_policy.title: Set a plus-one policy and apply it consistently
set_plus_one_policy.description: Pick a rule you can defend, such as married, engaged, or living together, and hold it. Exceptions are what start arguments.

negotiate_family_additions.title: Negotiate the family additions
negotiate_family_additions.description: If a parent is contributing money, expect a list. Agree on how many names, not which ones, and let them fill it.

collect_addresses.title: Collect mailing addresses
collect_addresses.description: Slower than you expect. Start before you think you need to.

lock_final_list.title: Lock the final list and count

budget_open_plus_ones.title: Add every open plus-one seat to the working count
budget_open_plus_ones.description: Treat each invitation as two seats until the RSVP says otherwise. Open plus-ones are generous only when their cost and capacity are real in the plan.

name_established_partners.title: Name every established partner on the invitation
name_established_partners.description: A known partner is a guest, not an unnamed plus-one. Check names and spelling instead of writing 'and guest.'

review_plus_one_exceptions.title: Review plus-one exceptions against one written rule
review_plus_one_exceptions.description: Check travel, social comfort, relationship context, and capacity. Write the reason so similar guests are treated consistently.

word_no_plus_one_invitations.title: Word named-guest invitations consistently
word_no_plus_one_invitations.description: List only invited names and make RSVP capacity match. Prepare one kind response for guests who ask to add someone.

count_children_and_plan_seating.title: Count children by age and plan where they sit
count_children_and_plan_seating.description: Ask the caterer about meals and high chairs, keep young children with caregivers, and include them in venue capacity.

list_kid_exceptions_by_household.title: List immediate-family child exceptions by household
list_kid_exceptions_by_household.description: Name the invited children rather than relying on guests to infer the exception. Use the same explanation with every household.

set_and_publish_age_cutoff.title: Choose one age cutoff and publish it clearly
set_and_publish_age_cutoff.description: Apply the cutoff by age on the wedding date, then name invited teens or children on each invitation.

word_adults_only_consistently.title: Use one clear adults-only message everywhere
word_adults_only_consistently.description: Address only invited adults, match RSVP capacity, and repeat the policy on the website without blaming the venue unless that is true.

add_travel_and_dress_code.title: Add travel, lodging, and dress code
add_travel_and_dress_code.description: Spell the dress code out in plain words. Guests search it anyway, and they guess wrong.

link_registry.title: Link the registry from the website, not the invitation

send_save_the_dates.title: Send save-the-dates
send_save_the_dates.description: Six to eight months out, or nine to twelve for guests traveling internationally.

order_invitations.title: Order invitations
order_invitations.description: Printing takes 3 to 6 weeks, and calligraphy adds more. Order enough for reprints and keepsakes.

mail_invitations.title: Mail the invitations
mail_invitations.description: Six to eight weeks before the wedding. Weigh a full suite at the post office first.

choose_digital_invitation_platform.title: Choose the digital invitation and RSVP platform
choose_digital_invitation_platform.description: Check mobile usability, household grouping, meal questions, reminders, exports, privacy, and whether you can correct a guest record without starting over.

test_digital_delivery_and_rsvp.title: Test the full digital invitation and RSVP flow
test_digital_delivery_and_rsvp.description: Send it to both of yourselves on different devices, complete every guest path, and confirm the answers export correctly.

plan_offline_guest_backup.title: Plan a personal backup for guests who will miss a digital invitation
plan_offline_guest_backup.description: Identify guests without reliable email or internet access and assign someone to call them and record the RSVP.

build_digital_rsvp_flow.title: Connect the paper invitation to a tested digital RSVP
build_digital_rsvp_flow.description: Use a short URL and optional QR code, test household lookup, and include a phone or mail alternative for guests who need it.

set_rsvp_deadline.title: Set an RSVP deadline
set_rsvp_deadline.description: Three to four weeks before, so it lands before your caterer's final headcount.

chase_rsvps.title: Chase the people who haven't replied
chase_rsvps.description: Roughly a quarter of guests will need a personal nudge. Split the list between you.

plus_one_policy.help: The kindest policy is one you can afford, explain, and apply consistently. Known partners should be invited by name rather than treated as interchangeable guests.

option.all_adults: Every adult guest may bring someone
option.case_by_case: We will decide by guest circumstance
option.no_plus_ones: Only the people named are invited

kids_policy.help: A clear household or age rule is easier for guests than exceptions they discover later. Immediate-family children can be an explicit exception.

invitation_format.prompt: How do you want invitations and RSVPs to work?
invitation_format.help: Paper carries ceremony and keepsake value. Digital reduces printing and makes corrections easier. A hybrid uses paper for the invitation and the website for RSVP data.

guest_experience.title: Guest Experience and Travel
guest_experience.subtitle: Taking care of the people who traveled for you
guest_experience.celebration: Your guests will be looked after before they even arrive.

block_hotel_rooms.title: Block hotel rooms
block_hotel_rooms.description: Blocks are usually free to hold. Get two options at different price points.

share_booking_links.title: Put booking links on the wedding website

watch_block_release_date.title: Note when unbooked rooms get released
watch_block_release_date.description: Usually about a month out. Remind guests before you lose the rate.

estimate_domestic_room_demand.title: Estimate room demand by household
estimate_domestic_room_demand.description: Ask likely travelers about dates, room count, accessibility, and price range before signing a block that does not fit them.

map_international_arrival_needs.title: Map international arrivals and extra-night needs
map_international_arrival_needs.description: Record airports, likely arrival days, time zones, room nights, language needs, and which households may need personal help.

confirm_lodging_help_not_needed.title: Confirm that guests do not need hosted lodging help
confirm_lodging_help_not_needed.description: Check for the few exceptions before skipping hotel blocks, then share a short list of nearby options only if someone asks.

arrange_shuttles.title: Arrange shuttles
arrange_shuttles.description: Worth it whenever there is an open bar and any distance to hotels.

plan_couple_transport.title: Sort out how the two of you get around

plan_late_night_rides.title: Plan how guests get home at the end

publish_walkable_route_and_accessibility.title: Publish the walkable route and accessibility details
publish_walkable_route_and_accessibility.description: Test the route yourself and share distance, surfaces, lighting, weather backup, transit hours, and an accessible alternative.

publish_parking_and_ride_details.title: Publish parking, rideshare, and designated-driver details
publish_parking_and_ride_details.description: Give exact addresses, parking cost and capacity, pickup zones, closing times, and a safe late-night option.

set_shuttle_schedule_and_capacity.title: Set the shuttle schedule, stops, and capacity
set_shuttle_schedule_and_capacity.description: Match seats to hotel demand, leave buffer for loading, and publish a final departure guests cannot misread.

map_transport_by_guest_need.title: Map transport by guest need
map_transport_by_guest_need.description: Separate guests who can walk or drive from those who need an accessible ride, a hotel shuttle, or late-night support.

write_area_guide.title: Write a short guide to the area

send_concise_arrival_guide.title: Send one concise arrival guide
send_concise_arrival_guide.description: Put the timeline, addresses, transport, weather, food nearby, and one contact in a mobile-friendly page instead of creating another event.

plan_drop_in_welcome.title: Plan a low-pressure drop-in welcome
plan_drop_in_welcome.description: Choose a clear window and easy location, keep attendance optional, and avoid turning arrival day into another formal obligation.

send_early_stds_overseas.title: Send save-the-dates to international guests first
send_early_stds_overseas.description: Nine to twelve months out. They need time for flights, time off, and possibly visas.

write_visa_invitation_letters.title: Write visa invitation letters
write_visa_invitation_letters.description: Some consulates require a formal invitation letter. Ask early, these can take months.

check_guest_passport_validity.title: Remind traveling guests to check passport validity

guest_mix.prompt: How much travel support will your guests actually need?
guest_mix.help: Bliss will add lodging and international logistics only when the guest mix creates them.

mobility_plan.prompt: How should guests move between lodging and the celebration?
mobility_plan.help: Choose the real access model. Safety, accessibility, parking, alcohol service, and the last trip of the night matter more than appearances.

option.walkable_transit: The route is walkable or transit-friendly
option.guest_self_transport: Guests will drive or use rideshare

welcome_level.prompt: What kind of welcome feels generous without over-scheduling everyone?
welcome_level.help: Hospitality can be excellent information, an optional hello, or a hosted event. More events are not automatically more caring.

option.guide_only: A thoughtful guide, no extra event

food_beverage.title: Food and Beverage
food_beverage.subtitle: The part your guests will actually remember
food_beverage.celebration: Menu set, bar sorted. Everyone is going to eat well.

choose_service_style.title: Choose a service style
choose_service_style.description: Plated is most formal and needs meal choices in advance. Buffet is usually cheaper but needs floor space. Family-style feels generous and costs closer to plated.

book_caterer.title: Book the caterer
book_caterer.description: Catering averages about $85 a person before service charge and gratuity.

collect_dietary_needs.title: Collect dietary restrictions and allergies
collect_dietary_needs.description: Ask on the RSVP card. Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, kosher, halal, and nut allergies at minimum.

budget_vendor_meals.title: Budget for vendor meals
budget_vendor_meals.description: Your contracts almost certainly require you to feed the photographer, band, and planner.

choose_bar_package.title: Choose a bar package
choose_bar_package.description: Open bar, limited bar, or consumption-based. A cash bar is widely considered poor form in the US.

check_corkage_and_byob.title: Check corkage fees or whether you can bring your own

pick_signature_drinks.title: Pick a signature drink or two

confirm_bartender_ratio.title: Confirm the bartender-to-guest ratio
confirm_bartender_ratio.description: One bartender per 50 guests keeps the line short.

check_cake_cutting_fee.title: Check the cake-cutting fee
check_cake_cutting_fee.description: Many venues charge per slice to serve a cake they did not make. It can rival the cake itself.

plan_dessert_table.title: Plan a dessert table or late-night snack

collect_meal_choices_with_rsvp.title: Collect meal choices with the RSVPs
collect_meal_choices_with_rsvp.description: A plated dinner needs every guest's selection before the caterer's deadline. Put the choices on the RSVP card and in the website form.

build_meal_key_for_place_cards.title: Build the meal key for the place cards
build_meal_key_for_place_cards.description: Servers need to know who gets what without asking. A small symbol or colored dot on each place card is the standard answer.

confirm_line_count_and_flow.title: Confirm how many serving lines and where they go
confirm_line_count_and_flow.description: One line for 150 guests means people eating forty minutes apart. Two lines, entered from both sides, is usually the fix.

confirm_platters_per_table.title: Confirm the number of platters per table
confirm_platters_per_table.description: Family style is priced per platter, not per plate, and tables of ten need more than tables of eight. Confirm it against the final floor plan.

plan_nonalcoholic_menu.title: Plan drinks for the people not drinking
plan_nonalcoholic_menu.description: Pregnant guests, sober guests, kids, and drivers are a real share of the room. Two good non-alcoholic options beat soda from a gun.

buy_alcohol_and_estimate_quantities.title: Buy the alcohol and estimate quantities
buy_alcohol_and_estimate_quantities.description: Plan on roughly one drink per guest per hour, heavier in the first hour. Buy on a return policy if the store offers one.

hire_licensed_bartender.title: Hire a licensed, insured bartender
hire_licensed_bartender.description: Most venues require it even when you supply the alcohol, and it is what keeps liability off you if a guest overdoes it.

service_style.help: This decides whether your RSVP card needs a meal choice and whether your place cards need a meal indicator. Getting it wrong means reprinting stationery.

bar_package.help: BYOB looks cheaper and is more work: you buy, transport, chill, and staff it, and most venues still require a licensed bartender.

option.limited_bar: Beer, wine, and a signature drink

dessert.prompt: Cake, a dessert table, or both?

design_flowers.title: Design, Flowers, and Rentals
design_flowers.subtitle: How the room will feel when they walk in
design_flowers.celebration: The look is locked. You already know what it will feel like to stand in it.

set_decor_budget.title: Set the decor and floral budget
set_decor_budget.description: Florals average around $2,900 and typically run 8 to 10% of the total.

map_immersive_design_zones.title: Map the full guest journey into design zones
map_immersive_design_zones.description: Prioritize arrival, ceremony, cocktails, dinner, and dancing as one atmosphere, then assign budget and one visual job to each zone.

choose_focal_design_moments.title: Choose the few design moments worth concentrating on
choose_focal_design_moments.description: Name two or three places guests will notice or photographs will preserve, and let the rest of the venue breathe.

write_minimal_design_rules.title: Write the rules for a deliberately minimal look
write_minimal_design_rules.description: Choose what stays, what disappears, and which venue features do the visual work so simplicity feels intentional rather than unfinished.

confirm_seasonal_availability.title: Confirm your flowers are in season
confirm_seasonal_availability.description: Out-of-season stems can cost several times more. A good florist will offer a lookalike.

finalize_floral_list.title: Finalize the floral list
finalize_floral_list.description: Bouquets, boutonnieres, corsages, centerpieces, ceremony arrangements, and any installation.

plan_flower_reuse.title: Plan to move ceremony flowers to the reception
plan_flower_reuse.description: The cheapest way to double your florals. Assign someone to actually move them.

write_fresh_floral_brief.title: Write the full fresh-floral brief
write_fresh_floral_brief.description: List every personal flower, arrangement, installation, vessel, delivery, move, and strike responsibility before comparing proposals.

approve_seasonal_substitution_rules.title: Approve seasonal substitution rules
approve_seasonal_substitution_rules.description: Define the color, texture, shape, and overall feeling the florist must preserve when a named stem is unavailable or unusually expensive.

design_low_flower_reuse_plan.title: Design a low-flower plan around reusable elements
design_low_flower_reuse_plan.description: Use greenery, plants, candles, vessels, produce, fabric, or rented objects where they create more impact and less waste than cut flowers.

design_non_floral_tablescape.title: Design the atmosphere without cut flowers
design_non_floral_tablescape.description: Build the visual system from lighting, linens, candles, objects, plants, paper, or venue architecture and check every open-flame rule.

confirm_what_venue_provides.title: Confirm what the venue already provides
confirm_what_venue_provides.description: Tables, chairs, linens, and glassware are often included. Do not rent them twice.

plan_lighting.title: Plan lighting
plan_lighting.description: Uplighting and string lights are the cheapest way to change how a room feels.

confirm_setup_strike_times.title: Confirm setup and strike windows
confirm_setup_strike_times.description: Ask when vendors can load in and when everything must be out. A tight strike window can cost you overtime.

confirm_full_service_install_plan.title: Confirm one full-service install and strike plan
confirm_full_service_install_plan.description: Name who owns delivery, placement, room flips, repacking, damage checks, and the last pickup so the couple is never the default crew.

write_vendor_diy_responsibility_matrix.title: Write the vendor and DIY responsibility matrix
write_vendor_diy_responsibility_matrix.description: Assign every object and every setup step to one owner. Anything with two assumed owners usually has no owner.

pack_and_label_diy_decor.title: Pack and label every DIY decor zone
pack_and_label_diy_decor.description: Use room-and-surface labels, a reference photo, inventory, and repacking instructions so helpers do not need to call you.

build_full_diy_setup_plan.title: Build the full DIY load-in, setup, and strike plan
build_full_diy_setup_plan.description: Time the work, vehicle loads, access windows, tools, ladders, storage, cleanup, and return trips before deciding the savings are real.

recruit_diy_setup_and_strike_crew.title: Recruit a willing DIY setup and strike crew
recruit_diy_setup_and_strike_crew.description: Ask named people for bounded shifts and get a clear yes. Wedding-party titles do not automatically make anyone the decor crew.

mock_up_and_inventory_diy_decor.title: Mock up and inventory every DIY decor element
mock_up_and_inventory_diy_decor.description: Build one complete sample, photograph it, count every component, and confirm the design works at venue scale before producing the rest.

design_escort_display.title: Design the escort card display
design_escort_display.description: Escort cards send guests to a table. Place cards assign a specific seat. You may want both.

plan_guest_book.title: Choose a guest book or alternative

scope.prompt: How much of the space should design transform?
scope.help: Choose where atmosphere earns its budget. A few concentrated moments can feel more intentional than decorating every available surface.

option.immersive: An immersive atmosphere across the whole guest journey

floral_approach.prompt: What role should flowers play in the design?
floral_approach.help: Bliss will separate the feeling you want from any specific stem, then add the sourcing and reuse work that choice creates.

option.fresh_full_service: Fresh flowers are a major design element

production_owner.help: DIY changes labor, transport, storage, access, and cleanup. Bliss will count that work instead of treating it as free.

option.split_vendor_diy: Vendors plus a bounded DIY portion
option.couple_diy: Mostly us and our chosen helpers

ceremony.title: Ceremony
ceremony.subtitle: The twenty minutes the whole day is built around
ceremony.celebration: The ceremony is written. This is the part you will remember word for word.

draft_ceremony_script.title: Draft the script with your officiant

write_vows.title: Write your vows
write_vows.description: If you are writing your own, agree on length and tone first so they match on the day.

confirm_traditional_ceremony_elements.title: Confirm the traditional ceremony elements you want to keep
confirm_traditional_ceremony_elements.description: List the required words, order, people, symbols, and permissions, then distinguish meaningful tradition from habit you do not need.

interview_each_other_for_ceremony_story.title: Give the officiant the stories only the two of you can tell
interview_each_other_for_ceremony_story.description: Answer the same prompts separately so the ceremony reflects specific moments, values, and humor instead of a generic love story.

map_blended_ceremony_elements.title: Map both traditions into one coherent ceremony
map_blended_ceremony_elements.description: Name the meaning, owner, order, language, objects, and family expectations for each element before deciding how they meet.

share_public_vows_for_timing.title: Share public vows for length and tone, not approval
share_public_vows_for_timing.description: Use a trusted reader or officiant to check timing and accidental mismatch while preserving the words as each person's own.

plan_private_vow_exchange.title: Plan a private vow exchange
plan_private_vow_exchange.description: Choose the time, place, privacy, photography boundary, and what simple promise will still be spoken during the ceremony.

select_guided_vow_language.title: Select guided or traditional vow language together
select_guided_vow_language.description: Read every line aloud, remove language that does not fit your relationship, and confirm whether you repeat or answer.

ask_readers.title: Ask your readers, and send them the text

plan_interfaith_blend.title: Plan how two traditions fit together
plan_interfaith_blend.description: Decide the order of rituals early. This is usually a family conversation, not a logistics one.

brief_both_officiants.title: Introduce both officiants to each other

choose_ceremony_music.title: Choose ceremony music
choose_ceremony_music.description: Prelude, processional, recessional. Confirm who is playing it and how it is amplified.

confirm_ceremony_sound.title: Confirm ceremony sound
confirm_ceremony_sound.description: Outdoor ceremonies need microphones. Guests in the back hearing nothing is the most common ceremony regret.

decide_unplugged.title: Decide whether to ask guests to put phones away

communicate_phone_free_ceremony.title: Communicate a fully phone-free ceremony
communicate_phone_free_ceremony.description: Put the request before guests arrive, repeat it once warmly, and let the officiant say when phones can come back out.

designate_vow_photo_boundary.title: Ask guests to put phones away for the vows
designate_vow_photo_boundary.description: Give one clear start and end to the private part so guests can participate without wondering whether the rule lasts all ceremony.

publish_respectful_guest_photo_rules.title: Publish respectful guest-photo boundaries
publish_respectful_guest_photo_rules.description: Welcome photos while protecting aisles, professional sightlines, private moments, and the couple's choice about social posting.

structure.prompt: What should hold the ceremony together?
structure.help: Bliss will protect the meaning you choose, whether that comes from a known tradition, your shared story, or a careful blend of both.

vow_format.prompt: Where should your most personal vows live?
vow_format.help: Private is not less meaningful, and guided language is not less sincere. Choose the setting where both people can be fully present.

guest_photos.prompt: When should guests be invited to take photos?
guest_photos.help: A precise boundary is kinder than a vague unplugged sign. Bliss will turn the choice into consistent wording and timing.

registry_rings_honeymoon.title: Registry, Rings, and Honeymoon
registry_rings_honeymoon.subtitle: The parts that are just for the two of you
registry_rings_honeymoon.celebration: Rings ordered, registry live, and something to look forward to after.

set_ring_budget.title: Set a budget for the bands
set_ring_budget.description: Rings typically run about 4% of the total budget.

order_bands.title: Order the bands
order_bands.description: Custom or engraved bands take 4 to 8 weeks. Resizing adds more.

insure_rings.title: Add the rings to your insurance

confirm_ready_made_stock_and_sizing.title: Confirm stock, sizing, and the return window
confirm_ready_made_stock_and_sizing.description: Try the exact width and profile, confirm whether the size is stocked or ordered, and leave time for one adjustment.

approve_custom_ring_design.title: Approve the custom ring design and production milestones
approve_custom_ring_design.description: Confirm dimensions, metal, stones, comfort, finish, engraving, resize limits, deposit, wax or CAD review, and final delivery date.

assess_heirloom_resize_and_restoration.title: Assess the heirloom rings for resizing and restoration
assess_heirloom_resize_and_restoration.description: Ask a qualified jeweler about metal condition, stone security, sizing limits, repairs, cleaning, insurance value, and how alterations affect history.

record_heirloom_ring_story.title: Record the story carried by the heirloom rings
record_heirloom_ring_story.description: Save who wore them, what they meant, what changed, and why the two of you chose to carry them forward.

add_range_of_price_points.title: Include a range of price points
add_range_of_price_points.description: Guests want options under $50 and over $200. Leaving out either makes people uncomfortable.

add_cash_funds.title: Add cash funds or a honeymoon fund

audit_home_and_life_needs.title: Audit what your home and shared life actually need
audit_home_and_life_needs.description: Replace the inherited checklist with items you will use, upgrades worth making, experiences you value, and things you already have enough of.

write_specific_fund_descriptions.title: Write specific, warm fund descriptions
write_specific_fund_descriptions.description: Explain what each contribution supports without pretending cash is an object. Keep amounts varied and make every gift optional.

publish_no_gifts_message.title: Publish a clear no-gifts message
publish_no_gifts_message.description: Say that their presence is enough, avoid adding a hidden alternative, and give close family the same answer so guests hear one consistent message.

check_passport_validity.title: Check passport validity
check_passport_validity.description: Many countries require six months of remaining validity. Renewals take weeks.

protect_post_wedding_departure_buffer.title: Protect a realistic buffer before departure
protect_post_wedding_departure_buffer.description: Leave time for sleep, returns, documents, luggage, weather, and one delayed flight instead of turning the wedding night into an airport deadline.

set_delayed_trip_savings_timeline.title: Set the delayed honeymoon date and savings timeline
set_delayed_trip_savings_timeline.description: Give the later trip a real month, budget, savings cadence, and booking checkpoint so delayed does not quietly become never.

plan_simple_mini_moon.title: Plan a simple mini-moon
plan_simple_mini_moon.description: Choose recovery and time together over itinerary density, with travel short enough that the trip still feels restful.

park_honeymoon_without_pressure.title: Park the honeymoon without creating another deadline
park_honeymoon_without_pressure.description: Record what is unresolved and choose one future month to revisit it. The marriage does not need a trip attached to the wedding.

ring_plan.prompt: What should your wedding rings carry: a new choice, a custom design, or an existing story?
ring_plan.help: Bliss will add only the sourcing, lead time, restoration, and story work your choice creates.

registry_style.prompt: What kind of gifting, if any, feels right?
registry_style.help: A registry is guest guidance, not an obligation. Choose objects, funds, both, or a consistent no-gifts message.

option.objects: Objects for our home and life
option.objects_and_funds: A mix of objects and funds

honeymoon_timing.prompt: What should happen after the wedding?
honeymoon_timing.help: A delayed trip, a small nearby break, or no current plan can be a better fit than leaving exhausted the next morning.

option.immediate_trip: Leave for a honeymoon soon after

legal.title: Legal and Paperwork
legal.subtitle: The part that makes it a marriage, not just a party
legal.celebration: Legally sorted. Everything else is celebration.

look_up_county_rules.title: Find the official office that issues your license
look_up_county_rules.description: Use the government source for the ceremony jurisdiction. The issuing office, process, waiting period, validity window, and document requirements can vary.

gather_license_documents.title: Gather the documents you need
gather_license_documents.description: Use the current checklist published by the issuing clerk. Do not rely on a generic document list, because requirements vary by jurisdiction and personal history.

translate_foreign_documents.title: Arrange any translation or certification the clerk confirms
translate_foreign_documents.description: Ask the issuing clerk which foreign documents they accept, whether translation must be certified, and whether originals or apostilles are required before paying a provider.

book_clerk_appointment.title: Follow the clerk's current application and appointment process
book_clerk_appointment.description: Confirm online and in-person steps, who must appear, fees, accepted payment, office hours, and appointment availability on the official clerk site.

observe_waiting_period.title: Account for the waiting period
observe_waiting_period.description: Use a verified state or county rule to calculate the earliest valid ceremony time and confirm whether any exception applies to you.

check_license_expiry.title: Check the expiry window
check_license_expiry.description: Confirm the current validity window with the issuing clerk and obtain the license only when it will still be valid on the ceremony date.

confirm_standard_document_set_with_clerk.title: Confirm the standard document set with the issuing clerk
confirm_standard_document_set_with_clerk.description: Save the official checklist and verify every person's identification, age, residency, and prior-name requirements before the appointment.

collect_prior_marriage_records_for_clerk.title: Confirm and collect any prior-marriage records
collect_prior_marriage_records_for_clerk.description: Ask the issuing clerk exactly which decrees, dates, certified copies, or death records apply to your circumstances and how recent copies must be.

confirm_foreign_document_acceptance_with.title: Confirm how the clerk accepts foreign documents
confirm_foreign_document_acceptance_with.description: Get the answer from the issuing office in writing when possible, including originals, translation, certification, apostille, name matching, and return of documents.

verify_officiant_is_valid.title: Verify your officiant can legally marry you here
verify_officiant_is_valid.description: Use the current government rule for the ceremony jurisdiction. Do not rely only on the officiant's assurance or a generic ordination website.

line_up_witnesses.title: Confirm and line up the required witnesses
line_up_witnesses.description: Use the issuing office's current instructions for the exact number, eligibility, and signing requirements.

assign_license_carrier.title: Assign one person to bring the license
assign_license_carrier.description: Not you. Give it to the person least likely to be distracted.

confirm_license_return.title: Confirm who files the signed license and by when
confirm_license_return.description: Follow the issuing office's current return instructions, assign the responsible person explicitly, and keep proof of timely filing.

order_certified_copies.title: Order certified copies of the marriage certificate
order_certified_copies.description: Estimate the copies required by your actual name, benefits, immigration, insurance, or records plan, then use the official ordering process.

change_name_social_security.title: Update the Social Security record if your plan requires it
change_name_social_security.description: Check the current Social Security Administration process, evidence, timing, and whether an appointment is required before changing downstream records.

change_name_drivers_license.title: Update the driver's license or state ID

change_name_passport.title: Update the passport and trusted-traveler records

change_name_banks_and_work.title: Update employer, banks, insurance, and other accounts

confirm_no_name_change_workflow.title: Confirm that neither partner wants a legal name-change workflow
confirm_no_name_change_workflow.description: Keep certified-copy and benefits tasks that still apply, but remove the assumption that marriage requires either person to change a name.

map_one_partner_name_change_accounts.title: Map one partner's name-change records and dependencies
map_one_partner_name_change_accounts.description: List government identity, work, travel, financial, health, property, professional, and digital records before starting so timing conflicts are visible.

map_both_partner_name_change_accounts.title: Map both partners' name-change paths separately
map_both_partner_name_change_accounts.description: Confirm that the chosen name is legally available in your jurisdiction, then track each person's evidence, agencies, accounts, and travel timing independently.

note_k1_ninety_day_window.title: Verify the current K-1 marriage deadline
note_k1_ninety_day_window.description: Use current USCIS instructions and qualified immigration counsel to confirm which deadline and evidence apply to the actual entry and status.

consult_immigration_attorney.title: Talk to an immigration attorney if status is involved
consult_immigration_attorney.description: Bliss provides general information, never legal advice.

prepare_questions_for_immigration_counse.title: Prepare a dated timeline and questions for immigration counsel
prepare_questions_for_immigration_counse.description: Bring entry, status, filing, travel, employment, prior-marriage, ceremony, and document facts without uploading sensitive identifiers into Bliss.

document_context.prompt: Which document path should the official clerk checklist cover?
document_context.help: This only organizes verification work. Bliss will not infer requirements; the issuing clerk's current rules remain the source of truth.

option.prior_marriage_records: A prior marriage may require records
option.foreign_documents: One or more documents were issued abroad

name_plan.prompt: Is either partner choosing a legal name change?
name_plan.help: Marriage does not require a name change. Bliss will create separate record workflows only for the people who choose one.

option.keep_names: Neither of us is changing a legal name
option.one_partner_changes: One partner plans to change a name
option.both_change_or_new_name: Both partners may change or create a new name

immigration_context.prompt: Does immigration status affect the timing or paperwork?
immigration_context.help: This shared workspace is not a place for passport numbers, receipt numbers, or case details. Bliss will only add a counsel workflow and never provide immigration advice.

option.k1_or_fiance_visa: A K-1 or fiancé-visa timeline may apply
option.other_status_or_unsure: Another status is involved, or we are unsure

pre_wedding_events.title: Pre-Wedding Events
pre_wedding_events.subtitle: Everything that happens before the main event
pre_wedding_events.celebration: The lead-up is planned. Now you get to enjoy it.

coordinate_showers.title: Coordinate with whoever is hosting a shower
coordinate_showers.description: Traditionally you do not host your own. Your job is to supply the guest list and stay out of it.

protect_no_extra_events_boundary.title: Tell family and friends you are not adding pre-wedding events
protect_no_extra_events_boundary.description: Use one warm, consistent answer and protect time, travel, spending, and attention for the wedding and the life around it.

set_boundaries_for_events_others_host.title: Set boundaries for events other people offer to host
set_boundaries_for_events_others_host.description: Agree on availability, guest-list control, cost expectations, gifts, accessibility, surprises, and what the couple is not taking on.

plan_one_joint_pre_wedding_gathering.title: Plan one shared pre-wedding gathering
plan_one_joint_pre_wedding_gathering.description: Bring the people and purposes together in one event instead of inheriting separate gendered or family-specific obligations.

map_event_calendar_and_guest_overlap.title: Map the event calendar, travel, gifts, and guest overlap
map_event_calendar_and_guest_overlap.description: Check who is repeatedly invited to spend, travel, or take time off, then remove or combine events before invitations go out.

book_rehearsal_time.title: Book rehearsal time at the venue
book_rehearsal_time.description: Confirm it in the venue contract. Rehearsal access is not always automatic.

decide_rehearsal_guest_list.title: Decide who comes to the rehearsal dinner
decide_rehearsal_guest_list.description: Wedding party, immediate family, officiant, and often out-of-town guests.

plan_toasts.title: Decide who is speaking, and when

plan_casual_post_rehearsal_meal.title: Plan a casual meal after the rehearsal
plan_casual_post_rehearsal_meal.description: Choose an easy format, clear host, bounded guest list, and finish time without making the night before another reception.

communicate_rehearsal_only_plan.title: Communicate that the rehearsal has no hosted meal
communicate_rehearsal_only_plan.description: Give the rehearsal time and finish time early so participants can make their own dinner plans without an awkward surprise.

protect_unstructured_post_wedding_time.title: Protect unstructured time after the wedding
protect_unstructured_post_wedding_time.description: Tell guests there is no hosted closing event and leave the couple room to sleep, say goodbye naturally, return items, or simply be together.

coordinate_two_closing_events_without_ov.title: Coordinate the after-party and brunch as two distinct invitations
coordinate_two_closing_events_without_ov.description: Set hosts, budgets, access, transportation, finish and start times, and attendance expectations so nobody is silently committed to both.

lead_up.prompt: How much celebration should happen before the wedding?
lead_up.help: Every event adds guest spending, travel, attention, and coordination. Choose the amount that adds joy instead of obligation.

option.hosted_by_others: Only events other people freely host

rehearsal_hospitality.prompt: What should follow the ceremony rehearsal?
rehearsal_hospitality.help: The rehearsal is the required logistics. The hospitality around it can be formal, casual, or omitted with clear notice.

closing_events.prompt: Should the wedding have a hosted closing event?
closing_events.help: Protect sleep, travel, hosting energy, and budgets. Guests do not need another event in order to feel welcomed.

final_30_and_day_of.title: Final 30 Days and Day-Of
final_30_and_day_of.subtitle: Deep breath. This is the last stretch.
final_30_and_day_of.celebration: Everything is ready. Tomorrow you only have one job, and it is to enjoy it.

give_final_headcount.title: Give the caterer your final headcount
give_final_headcount.description: Usually due 7 to 10 days out. You pay for this number whether or not they show up.

build_seating_chart.title: Build the seating chart
build_seating_chart.description: Start earlier than feels necessary. It takes longer than anyone expects and changes until the last week.

confirm_dietary_counts.title: Confirm dietary counts and which seats they belong to

build_run_of_show.title: Build the run of show
build_run_of_show.description: A minute-by-minute schedule from hair and makeup to send-off, with names and phone numbers on it.

send_timeline_to_all_vendors.title: Send the run of show to every vendor

confirm_vendor_arrival_times.title: Confirm arrival times with each vendor individually

send_shot_list.title: Send the shot list and family photo groupings

plan_around_golden_hour.title: Build the timeline around golden hour
plan_around_golden_hour.description: The hour before sunset. Ask your photographer to name the exact time and protect fifteen minutes of it.

confirm_professional_command_chain.title: Confirm the professional day-of command chain
confirm_professional_command_chain.description: Name who makes schedule, vendor, setup, guest, weather, and emergency calls, then route every vendor and family contact through that chain.

brief_trusted_day_of_lead.title: Brief the trusted day-of lead and protect their boundaries
brief_trusted_day_of_lead.description: Give one willing person the timeline, contacts, authority, escalation rules, breaks, and a backup without making them responsible for every task.

reduce_and_assign_couple_led_decisions.title: Reduce and assign every remaining couple-led decision
reduce_and_assign_couple_led_decisions.description: Pre-decide what you can, split the rest, write who interrupts whom for what, and delegate anything that does not genuinely require the couple.

prepare_tip_envelopes.title: Prepare tip envelopes
prepare_tip_envelopes.description: Label each one. Gratuity is expected in the US and is separate from any service charge.

assign_someone_to_hand_out_tips.title: Give the envelopes to your point person, not to yourself

pack_emergency_kit.title: Pack an emergency kit
pack_emergency_kit.description: Safety pins, stain remover, blister pads, painkillers, deodorant, sewing kit, phone charger, snacks.

assign_item_carriers.title: Assign a person to every item that must arrive
assign_item_carriers.description: Rings, license, vows, cards, gifts, and the emergency kit. Each one gets a name.

confirm_weather_backup.title: Confirm the weather backup and when the call gets made

hand_off_to_point_person.title: Hand everything to your point person
hand_off_to_point_person.description: The last real task. After this, your only job is to be there.

confirm_indoor_access_and_climate.title: Confirm indoor access, climate, and emergency egress
confirm_indoor_access_and_climate.description: Check opening times, loading routes, heating or cooling, coat storage, elevators, accessibility, power, and who unlocks every space.

set_outdoor_weather_decision_deadline.title: Set the outdoor weather decision deadline and owner
set_outdoor_weather_decision_deadline.description: Name the forecast source, exact threshold, decision time, decision-maker, vendor notification tree, and guest communication channel.

map_weather_plan_by_space.title: Map the weather plan for each indoor and outdoor space
map_weather_plan_by_space.description: Decide separately for arrivals, ceremony, cocktails, portraits, dinner, and departure so one rain plan does not hide six different transitions.

preserve_the_gown.title: Send the gown for cleaning and preservation

write_thank_you_notes.title: Write thank-you notes
write_thank_you_notes.description: Within about three months. Split the list and do a few at a time.

order_album.title: Choose photos and order an album

confirm_delegated_closeout_manifest.title: Confirm the delegated closeout manifest
confirm_delegated_closeout_manifest.description: List every card, gift, rental, outfit, personal item, leftover, key, tip, vehicle, return deadline, storage location, and named recipient.

split_closeout_shifts_with_helpers.title: Split closeout into bounded shifts with willing helpers
split_closeout_shifts_with_helpers.description: Assign pickup, venue sweep, hotel delivery, returns, and next-day storage as separate jobs with clear finish points.

protect_couple_managed_closeout_buffer.title: Protect time and transport for couple-managed closeout
protect_couple_managed_closeout_buffer.description: Reserve vehicles, storage, return windows, sleep, and a next-day work block before accepting a plan that makes the couple the final cleanup crew.

coordination_handoff.prompt: Who runs the day once the timeline starts?
coordination_handoff.help: A real handoff means vendors and family stop treating the couple as the default decision desk.

option.trusted_person: A willing, trusted person with a backup
option.couple_led: The two of us, with tightly reduced decisions

weather_exposure.prompt: How many parts of the day depend on outdoor conditions?
weather_exposure.help: Bliss will create a decision deadline and owner only where weather can change the actual plan.

option.outdoor_with_backup: A main outdoor plan with an indoor backup
option.mixed_spaces: Different parts use indoor and outdoor spaces

closeout_owner.prompt: Who owns the objects, returns, and cleanup after the celebration?
closeout_owner.help: The wedding is not over when the music stops. Make the final load, storage, keys, cards, gifts, and returns visible before assigning them.

option.couple_managed: The two of us will manage closeout
